stem: A machine must be replaced at the end of 4 years. The replacement is expected to cost Rs 1,20,000 at that time, but the worn-out machine will then fetch a salvage of Rs 20,000, which will be put towards the new machine. To meet the balance, the firm sets aside an equal sum at the end of each year into a sinking fund earning 10% per annum compounded annually. What is the annual deposit? [Use: the future value of Re 1 deposited at the end of each year for 4 years at 10% = 4.641]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Derive the net amount to accumulate first: replacement cost 1,20,000 minus salvage 20,000 = 1,00,000. The sinking fund must grow to this, so deposit * 4.641 = 1,00,000, giving deposit = 1,00,000/4.641 = Rs 21,547.
Targets the gross 1,20,000 and forgets the salvage credit: 1,20,000/4.641 = 25,856. The Rs 20,000 that offsets the cost was not netted out.
Uses the correct net 1,00,000 but divides by the number of years 4 instead of the future-value factor 4.641: 1,00,000/4 = 25,000. This ignores the interest the early deposits earn.
Both errors at once: keeps the gross 1,20,000 and divides by 4 years, 1,20,000/4 = 30,000, ignoring salvage and ignoring interest. Two adjustments are missed.

explanation: A sinking-fund deposit must accumulate to the net outlay, so derive that first. The new machine costs 1,20,000 at the end of year 4, but the old machine's salvage of 20,000 is applied against it, leaving a net target of 1,20,000 - 20,000 = 1,00,000. Equal end-of-year deposits accumulate by the future-value factor: deposit * 4.641 = 1,00,000. Hence deposit = 1,00,000/4.641 = Rs 21,547.

explanation_sections.punchline: Find the net replacement cost before touching the sinking-fund formula: salvage offsets the bill, so the fund only has to reach Rs 1,00,000, not Rs 1,20,000.
explanation_sections.approach: For a sinking fund tied to an asset replacement, first net the future cost against any salvage or trade-in to get the true target. Then set deposit times the future-value-of-annuity factor equal to that target and solve for the deposit. The factor, not the year count, carries the interest the deposits earn.
explanation_sections.lesson: Sinking-fund target = future replacement cost minus salvage; divide by the FV-annuity factor, never by the plain number of years.
explanation_sections.timing: About 175 seconds. Fastest elimination: reject Rs 25,000, which divides the right net target by 4 years and so throws away all the interest the fund earns.
